title: Go where learning is (Avot 4:14)
hook: every lecture is online, so why go anywhere? Nehorai: exile yourself to a place of Torah
tomorrow: the wrong show won. is there an answer for why?

segments.voice: Last time, the crown above the crowns: a good name, built by how you treat people. Now a story about where you stand.

Every lecture is recorded now. Every tutorial is a search away. So can you learn it just as well from home? The Talmud answers with a story. There was a sage named Rabbi Elazar ben Arach, and his own teacher, in Avot, called him an ever-flowing spring. One day he went to a town known for its wine and its waters, and he liked it, and he stayed. When he finally came back, he was called up to read from the Torah in front of everyone. He opened the scroll. And the words came out wrong.
screen: `IT'S ALL ONLINE, RIGHT?` → `AN EVER-FLOWING SPRING.` → `THE WORDS CAME OUT WRONG.`

segments.voice: The verse was about the new month. He read it as something about a deaf heart, swapping letters that look alike. His learning, the Talmud says, had been forgotten. The sages prayed for him, and it came back. And right there the Talmud brings a saying from Pirkei Avot. Rabbi Nehorai says: exile yourself to a place of Torah. Don't say it will come after you. Your companions will make it firm in your hand. And don't lean on your own understanding. The Talmud even records a view that Nehorai was Elazar ben Arach himself, under another name. Here's the turn. The ever-flowing spring didn't lose his learning by being lazy. He lost it by being somewhere it wasn't, without the people who kept it alive. Learning, in this saying, isn't a file you carry. It's held in a place, by companions, the ones who argue with you and catch your mistakes. That's why Nehorai says go. Don't wait for it to come after you. Not every move has to be a big one: a study partner, a class, a table where people read together. Go where learning is.
screen: `HE READ IT WRONG.` · `EXILE YOURSELF TO A PLACE OF TORAH.` · `COMPANIONS MAKE IT FIRM.` · `IT WON'T COME AFTER YOU.` · then, large: `GO WHERE LEARNING IS.`

segments.voice: Stand up and walk, slowly, for about a minute, to the spot where you learn best: a desk, a chair by a window, a kitchen table. When you get there, sit down, and for the rest of the sit, think of the one person you'd most like learning across from you.
screen: `WALK TO WHERE YOU LEARN BEST.` · `SIT DOWN THERE.` · `WHO'S ACROSS FROM YOU?`

segments.voice: Go where learning is. Rabbi Nehorai: exile yourself to a place of Torah, and let your companions make it firm.
For the road: go where learning is, because it won't come after you. Thirty-seven of sixty, until tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 1464 COUNTS.` → `AVOT, CHAPTERS 3–6 · 37 OF 60.` → `TOMORROW: THE WRONG SHOW WON. IS THERE AN ANSWER FOR WHY?`

howItsDone: Many Jews learn in a beit midrash, a study hall, or with a chavruta, a study partner, and some leave home for a season or a year to study in a yeshiva or seminary.
